chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Mutamatti' (pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu') cuts off the Talbiyah when he looks at the houses of Mecca.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The ritual recitation of 'Labbayk' during Hajj or Umrah.
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season.
key_terms.بُيُوتِ مَكَّةَ: The houses of Mecca, referring specifically to the Kaaba and the surrounding structures.

ai.seo_question: When he looks at the houses of Mecca, he cuts off the Talbiyah.
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani's chain highlights the precise moment the Mutamatti' pilgrim concludes the Talbiyah upon sighting the houses of Mecca, a view held by many Shia jurists as the point of entering the sacred precincts. It underscores the ritual transition from the state of Ihram for Hajj to the commencement of Tawaf, distinguishing it from the Qarini who continues until reaching the Mataf. This ruling reflects the scholarly emphasis on the physical entry into Mecca as the marker for ending the initial invocation of arrival.
